title: Benchmarks are measurement instruments
summary: Reliability, invariance and validity ceilings for AI and agent benchmarks, measured on public item-level data, with a one-command tool that reports all three for any results file.

headline_numbers.label: Reliability of the SWE-bench Verified ranking, all 173 submissions vs top 20
headline_numbers.command: uv run python experiments/swebench.py  # results/swebench.json: population_curve[k=173].g, population_curve[k=20].g

headline_numbers.label: Top-10 reliability estimated naively on the same tasks vs with a task split
headline_numbers.command: uv run python experiments/swebench.py  # results/swebench.json: population_curve[k=10].naive_g and .g

headline_numbers.label: Adjacent top-20 SWE-bench Verified pairs separable by exact McNemar
headline_numbers.command: uv run python experiments/swebench.py  # results/swebench.json: pairs.top20.adjacent_separable

headline_numbers.label: True-score correlation, SWE-bench Verified vs Multilingual, 12 matched models
headline_numbers.value: 0.98 (coverage 0.96, 95% CI 0.63 to 1.00; 0.80 without the weakest model)
headline_numbers.command: uv run python experiments/swebench.py  # results/swebench.json: coverage_multilingual.r_true, .coverage, .ci_low, .ci_high, .without_weakest.coverage
